tagline: Every sentence has a heartbeat. Tap it, hear it, let it rest.

epigraph.text: 'Tis not enough no harshness gives offence, / The sound must seem an echo to the sense.
epigraph.cite: Alexander Pope, An Essay on Criticism (1711)

art.note: The council decided to keep the exhibit a static, tactile artifact with a breathing asymmetric grid, using negative space as rhythmic rest and wet-ink script for the primary handmade feel.

writers.note: Wet-ink whispers and open rests that let the reader tap, step, and breathe with the line.

nuggets.hook: A line can whisper, shout, or skip a beat.
nuggets.body: Tap along with the strong syllables. When the pattern breaks, your ear knows before your mind does.

nuggets.hook: Your feet know the rhythm before your eyes do.
nuggets.body: Marches, waltzes, and gallops hide in stressed syllables. Try walking a line of verse to feel its speed.

nuggets.hook: Some words chime even when they don't rhyme.
nuggets.body: Repeated vowels and consonants make a line hum. Listen for echoes that are not rhymes.

nuggets.hook: A sentence can hold its breath for one page.
nuggets.body: Long clauses stretch the pulse; short ones land like drums. Slow a line down to hear its hidden tempo.
